The menu-bar window opened on the other display, not under the icon
error: The menu-bar window opened on the other display, not under the icon
fix: Find the monitor containing the icon, use that monitor's scale, clamp to its edges, and set the position again after show (macOS converts the first move with the old screen's scale).
root_cause: The icon's rectangle was converted to physical pixels with the tray window's own scale factor, which is the scale of the screen it was last on; with two displays of different scale the position landed on the wrong screen.

detail: Choose… (a folder dialog) took about 20 seconds to open
error: Choose… (a folder dialog) took about 20 seconds to open
fix: src-tauri/src/folder_panel.rs keeps one NSOpenPanel for the app's life and reuses it; every folder button calls choose_folders instead of the dialog plugin's open().
root_cause: On macOS 27 a second NSOpenPanel in one process waits ~26 s in -[NSSavePanel _initBridgeAndStuff] on its out-of-process view service (measured in a bare Swift app: 0.5 s first, 26 s second; reusing the first panel is instant). tauri-plugin-dialog makes a new panel every time.

detail: Folder dialogs still waited 20-26 s, the first one of a run too, in Keepr and other non-sandboxed apps
error: Folder dialogs still waited 20-26 s, the first one of a run too, in Keepr and other non-sandboxed apps
fix: Nothing to change in Keepr beyond the reused panel; the stuck cloud provider has to be restarted or re-signed-in. Diagnose with: sample the openAndSavePanelService pid during the wait, and fileproviderctl dump.
root_cause: Not Keepr: the open-panel helper blocks in TNode::RootFPItemsForDomainsWithTimeout waiting for every File Provider domain's root item for the sidebar; a cloud domain whose extension isn't running (fileproviderctl dump shows it 'without connection' for the openAndSavePanelService servicers) makes every new panel wait out the timeout. Reusing one panel (folder_panel.rs) avoids the wait after the first.

detail: Slow folder dialogs on the dev Mac were fixed outside Keepr: restarting a disconnected cloud File Provider, then turning iCloud Drive on and off again (it was off while signed in to iCloud, and the panel waited on its root item). After that every new NSOpenPanel took under 0.6 s. Keepr keeps reusing one panel regardless.
The SMB dialogs didn't list a server's shares, and found no servers
error: The SMB dialogs didn't list a server's shares, and found no servers
fix: Shares show as buttons; -N goes before the server; Bonjour is browsed with DNSServiceBrowse directly; servers Keepr uses or has mounted are offered too (a network may have no SMB servers on Bonjour at all).
root_cause: Three things: shares went into an HTML datalist, which shows nothing until you type; for a guest login -N came after the server, where smbutil stops reading options; and dns-sd -B buffers its output when not writing to a terminal, so reading it for a second got nothing.

detail: Keepr can't write there: Operation not supported (os error 45) on an SMB share
error: Keepr can't write there: Operation not supported (os error 45) on an SMB share
fix: keepr_engine::backend::sync falls back to fsync(2) on ENOTSUP/EINVAL/ENOTTY; used by the backend, restore and the destination test. Confirmed on a real share: F_FULLFSYNC -> 45, fsync ok.
root_cause: On macOS, Rust's File::sync_all issues fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC), which smbfs refuses with ENOTSUP; the destination test, every pack and index write, and restores all called it.
